elements.content: Every time you switch tasks, your brain pays a time cost.
It feels fast, but you keep restarting.
Rubinstein et al., 2001 · J Exp Psych
people were slower when they switched
tasks than when they stuck with one.
And the harder the task, the bigger that cost.
One: pick one task, and set a twenty-minute timer you can see.
Two: phone face down, in another room if you can.
Three: when a new thought pops up, write it on a later list and keep going.
These were simple lab tasks, so real work varies,
and some jobs need quick switching.
Try it today: one task, one twenty-minute block, timer where you can see it.
